name: Dirac-Coulomb (Sommerfeld) energy levels E_{n kappa} = m [1 + (Z alpha/(n - |k| + sqrt(k^2 - Z^2 alpha^2)))^2]^{-1/2}

source.located: Primary: Sommerfeld, Ann. Phys. 51 (1916) 1 (old quantum theory); Dirac, Proc. R. Soc. A 117 (1928) 610; exact Dirac-theory solution by Darwin, Proc. R. Soc. A 118 (1928) 654 and Gordon, Z. Phys. 48 (1928) 11 -- none on arXiv. Read via restatement in: arXiv:2409.03787 (Mohr, Newell, Taylor, Tiesinga, CODATA 2022) p.10-11 eqs (26), (28)-(31), p.15-17 eqs (47)-(64), p.51 Table XXXIII; arXiv:2401.07485 (Suslov 2024, 'The Sommerfeld puzzle') p.1, 6-7 eqs (31)-(33); arXiv:2302.06288 (Kuzmenko, Kuzmenko, Avishai, Band 2023) p.1-5 eqs (1), (15)-(24), p.9-11 eqs (51), (61), Tables III, V.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text for all three arXiv papers. Sommerfeld 1916, Dirac 1928, Darwin 1928 and Gordon 1928 are NAMED-NOT-READ; the formula is taken from CODATA 2022 eqs (28)-(29) and Suslov eqs (31)-(32), which agree with each other and with excite.py:962-968.

published_statement: CODATA 2022 (2409.03787 p.11): 'The largest contribution to the electron energy, including its rest mass, is the Dirac eigenvalue for an electron bound to an infinitely heavy point nucleus, which is given by E_D = f(n, kappa) m_e c^2, (28) with f(n, kappa) = [1 + (Z alpha)^2/(n - delta)^2]^{-1/2} (29) where n is the principal quantum number, kappa = (-1)^{j-l+1/2}(j + 1/2) is the Dirac angular-momentum-parity quantum number ... and delta = |kappa| - sqrt(kappa^2 - (Z alpha)^2). States with the same n and j have degenerate eigenvalues.' Suslov (2401.07485 p.6-7 eqs 31-32): 'The relativistic energy levels of an electron in the central Coulomb field are given by [Darwin, Gordon, Sommerfeld]: E = mc^2/sqrt(1 + mu^2/(n_r + nu)^2) (n_r = 0, 1, 2, ...), mu = Ze^2/(hbar c), nu_Dirac = sqrt((j+1/2)^2 - mu^2)'; p.1: 'Exact solution was obtained by C. G. Darwin and W. Gordon only in 1928 after discovery of the Dirac equation: The new answer was precisely the old Sommerfeld formula!' Since n - delta = n - |kappa| + sqrt(kappa^2 - Z^2 alpha^2), this is identically excite.py's E_{n kappa}.
published_hypotheses: single electron obeying the Dirac equation in an external static Coulomb potential V = -Z e^2/r (Kuzmenko et al. eq 1)
point nucleus (CODATA 'point nucleus'; Kuzmenko p.1: 'If the proton ... is taken as a point charge, analytic expressions ... exist')

infinitely heavy nucleus (CODATA eq 28); a finite nuclear mass is handled separately by the reduced mass m_r and recoil terms in CODATA eqs (30)-(31), and Kuzmenko p.4 notes 'the concept of a reduced mass in the Dirac equation is ambiguous to some extent'

Z alpha < |kappa| so that gamma = sqrt(kappa^2 - Z^2 alpha^2) is real; Kuzmenko p.5: 'For Z > Z_max = 137 the parameter gamma becomes imaginary ... the Dirac equation with the Coulomb potential of a point-like nucleus is meaningful only for Z < 137'

quantum numbers: n_r = n - |kappa| = 0, 1, 2, ...; the n_r = 0 solution exists only for kappa < 0 (Kuzmenko p.4: 'In the special case gamma - Z alpha eps/lambda = 0, and kappa < 0, A_2 = 0'); kappa = -1, 1, -2, 2, -3 <-> S1/2, P1/2, P3/2, D3/2, D5/2 (CODATA p.11)

no QED radiative corrections, no hyperfine structure, no finite nuclear size or polarizability, no recoil: CODATA eq (26) E = -(E_h/2n^2)(1 + F) with F 'determined by QED, recoil corrections, etc.', and sections III.A.2-9 (relativistic recoil, self energy, vacuum polarization, two- and three-photon, finite nuclear size, radiative-recoil, nucleus self energy) are all corrections BEYOND the Dirac eigenvalue; hyperfine is 'not included here' (p.11)
hypothesis_drift: NONE on the load-bearing pair. excite.py:195-197 'point nuclei clamped' = CODATA's 'infinitely heavy point nucleus' (clamped = infinite mass, point = zero radius); excite.py:198 restricts the dilation claim to 'every dimensionless observable of THAT MODEL', i.e. it does not extend the result to real hydrogen, so dropping QED / hyperfine / nuclear size is a named model boundary, not a drift.

ADDED by the tree, not a source hypothesis: 'alpha fixed (H2)' (excite.py:195-196). It is the tree's own variation hypothesis for D18 (what moves when m_e moves); the source spectrum holds at any fixed alpha, so the addition is consistent and costs nothing.

DROPPED (inert at the use): the domain Z alpha < |kappa|. excite.py:962-968 dirac_level docstring and the sympy row V9c (excite.py:1819-1822, kk declared positive with no Za < kk condition) state the formula without it. At Z = 1 it is satisfied by all states (alpha = 0.0073 < 1); and math.sqrt raises ValueError outside it, so it cannot fail silently. Re-derivation R6.

DROPPED (inert at the use): 'n_r = 0 only for kappa < 0'. dirac_level (excite.py:962-968) returns a number for the non-existent n = 1, kappa = +1 state (re-derivation R1 DOMAIN row: the formula gives a value but the radial pair has NO eigenfunction, s_min = 2.0). The five states actually evaluated at excite.py:1601-1602, (1,-1), (2,-1), (2,1), (2,-2), (3,2), are all valid (R6).

NOT A DRIFT, a naming note: the canonical title says 'Dirac-Coulomb (Sommerfeld)'. Per Suslov p.1, 7, the formula is Sommerfeld's 1916 result and was obtained exactly from the Dirac equation by Darwin and Gordon (1928); Schrodinger's letter (Suslov p.7) calls the coincidence 'fortuitous'. The tree attributes nothing further, so there is no misattribution.

data_at_publication.quantity: fine-structure constant alpha (the only numerical input of the formula; Z = 1)
data_at_publication.value_then: tree: 1/alpha = 137.035999084 (address.py:429, marked 'CODATA NAMED-NOT-READ'; this is the CODATA 2018 value). At the formula's publication (1916/1928) alpha^-1 ~ 137 was known to ~1e-3; the formula is exact in alpha and uses no measured value.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: NO. The tree's conclusion is E/m independent of m (D18 spectrum side), which holds identically for every alpha in the domain: re-derivation R4 (sympy, exact) and R7 (60-digit E(2m)/E(m) = 2 to < 1e-55 under both 2018 and 2022 alpha). The absolute binding energies move by relative -1.36e-9 (R7), which no statement of the tree uses. The domain edge Z_max = floor(1/alpha) = 137 is unchanged (R6).

data_at_publication.quantity: E(2m)/E(m) at five (n, kappa) (excite.py:1601-1605, the tree's recorded check '= 2 to 1e-15')
data_at_publication.value_now: re-derived: exactly 2.0 in IEEE float (R5), and 2 to < 1e-55 at 60 digits (R7)
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: NO -- but a discrepancy of evidential weight is recorded (not an error): multiplying by 2.0 is an exact binary scaling, so the float check passes for ANY function of the form m*f(alpha), including a wrong spectrum (R5 CONTROL). It tests linearity of the code in m, not the spectrum. The substantive evidence is the tree's own --verify V9a/V9b/V9c (sympy, all 0; control C9 fires), reproduced independently here (R4) and run as-is in this audit.

data_at_publication.quantity: proton charge radius r_p (enters only the named-away finite-size correction)
data_at_publication.value_then: not used by the tree (point nucleus is a named hypothesis)
data_at_publication.value_now: 0.84075 fm used in R8 for scale only -- NAMED-NOT-READ (Kuzmenko et al. p.1 quote CODATA 2018 r_p = 0.8414(19) fm, READ); not load-bearing: the conclusion of R8 is an order of magnitude
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: NO for the tree's model statement. For real hydrogen a fixed-radius nucleus breaks the exact dilation: E_nucl^(4) propto m^3 r_N^2 (CODATA eq 50), 3.37e-10 of the 1S binding, so m -> m(1+1e-2) moves 1S binding/m by 6.8e-12 beyond the dilation (R8). This is the price of the named hypothesis 'point nucleus', and it is small; the tree does not claim otherwise.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0, ~14 s). R1: in the tree's own sign convention (excite.py:1811-1812) the formula is an exact eigenvalue of the radial Dirac-Coulomb pair -- polynomial x r^gamma e^{-lambda r} eigenfunctions for n_r = 0 (1s, 2p3/2, 3d5/2) and n_r = 1 (2s, 2p1/2, 3d3/2, 3p3/2), smallest singular value of the coefficient system <= 1.8e-63 at 60 digits, also at Z alpha = 1/2; CONTROLS fire: the Klein-Gordon level (s_min 1.4e-7) and a shifted n_r (2.6e-3) are not eigenvalues, and n=1 kappa=+1 has no eigenfunction (s_min 2.0). R2: independent RK4 shooting at 1/alpha = 137.035999177 brackets the formula's E within 1e-4 of the binding for all five states excite.py evaluates. R3: the mu -> 0 expansion equals Suslov eq (33) exactly. R4: E(lambda m) = lambda E(m) and d ln E/d ln m = 1 exactly; the radial pair is m-free after r = x/m (reproduces the tree's V9a/V9b/V9c, which were also run as-is: all 0, control C9 NONZERO). R5: the float ratio check is exact binary scaling and passes for a wrong spectrum too (control). R6: domain respected at every use. R7: alpha 2018 -> 2022 leaves the ratio at 2. R8: finite nuclear size breaks the dilation at 6.8e-12 for eps = 1e-2.

later_literature.what: States the Dirac eigenvalue exactly as the tree does (eqs 28-29) under 'infinitely heavy point nucleus', and uses it as the leading term of the adjusted hydrogen theory; lists every correction beyond it (recoil, self energy, vacuum polarization, 2- and 3-photon, finite size, radiative recoil, nucleus self energy) -- extending, not contradicting, the model. Also supplies the current alpha.

later_literature.ref: arXiv:2401.07485 (Suslov 2024, The Sommerfeld puzzle and its extensions)
later_literature.what: Re-derives the Dirac-Coulomb levels (eq 31-32) and the Sommerfeld/Dirac coincidence; gives the nonrelativistic expansion eq (33) reproduced exactly in R3; history: exact Dirac solution by Darwin and Gordon 1928.

The point-Coulomb Dirac problem 'is meaningful only for Z < 137' (p.5); nuclei are not points, and finite-nuclear-size corrections are 1.68e-10 Hartree for H 1s and per the abstract 'comparable to the relativistic QED radiative corrections for the light nuclei, but much larger than both these corrections for heavy nuclei' (Table III: 7.3 Hartree for U 1s). Narrows the formula's physical validity to light, point-like nuclei -- exactly the class the tree uses (Z = 1, point nucleus named).
Recoil corrections beyond the clamped-nucleus Dirac eigenvalue; relevant only if the 'clamped' hypothesis is lifted (the tree routes m_p/m_e through K_mu separately).

lacked_data: What the 1916/1928 authors lacked: the Lamb shift and all QED radiative corrections (post-1947), the finite proton radius (and its muonic-hydrogen re-measurement), the hyperfine/recoil theory, and alpha beyond ~1e-3. Evidence that this data changes the physics of real hydrogen: CODATA 2022 eq (26) and Sec. III.A.2-9 (READ) add corrections beyond the Dirac eigenvalue, and nS1/2 and nP1/2 are no longer degenerate once a finite nuclear mass enters (CODATA p.11: 'In these equations the energy of nS1/2 states differs from that of nP1/2 states'). Evidence that it does NOT change the result AS THE TREE USES IT: (i) the formula is an exact eigenvalue theorem of the stated model, re-derived here by two independent routes (R1 exact eigenfunctions with controls, R2 numerical shooting) -- no datum enters it but alpha; (ii) the tree's conclusion (E/m m-independent, D18 spectrum side) holds at every alpha (R4, R7), and the one datum that has moved, 1/alpha 2018 -> 2022 by 4.4 sigma of the 2022 uncertainty, leaves E(2m)/E(m) = 2 to < 1e-55; (iii) the tree confines its claim to 'that model' with 'point nuclei clamped' named, and the largest effect a real nucleus adds under a dilation (finite size) is computed at 6.8e-12 for eps = 1e-2 (R8). M's hypothesis is therefore answered NO for this result: the later data completes the model of real hydrogen but neither contradicts the model's spectrum nor moves the tree's inference from it. Not computed here: whether QED loops with other charged species (muon/hadron vacuum polarization, carrying m_e/m_mu) break the dilation when only m_e moves -- the tree does not claim it for them, so this is recorded as outside the use, not as a finding.
grade_evidence: Statement READ at source via restatement (CODATA 2022 eqs 28-29; Suslov eqs 31-32) and identical to excite.py:962-968. Hypotheses as used ('point nucleus clamped' = 'infinitely heavy point nucleus'; claim restricted to 'that model', excite.py:195-198) match the source; the two dropped domain conditions (Z alpha < |kappa|; n_r = 0 only for kappa < 0) are satisfied at every evaluation the tree makes (R6) and fail loudly or are never reached. Re-derivation agrees: exact eigenfunctions in the tree's own sign convention with three controls firing (R1), independent RK4 shooting (R2), NR limit (R3), exact m-homogeneity of spectrum and radial pair (R4; the tree's own --verify V9a/b/c run as-is: 0, 0, 0, control C9 fires). The only moved datum (alpha, CODATA 2018 -> 2022) does not move the conclusion (R7). Recorded discrepancy, not an error: the float check at excite.py:1601-1605 is exact binary scaling and would pass for a wrong spectrum (R5), so its evidential weight is nil; the result's support rests on --verify V9, which holds.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree extended D18 beyond the point-nucleus Dirac-Coulomb model to real hydrogen observables (finite nuclear size breaks the exact dilation at a computed 6.8e-12 for eps = 1e-2; recoil and non-electron QED loops would need their own analysis), or if a use evaluated dirac_level at Z alpha >= |kappa| or at a kappa > 0, n = |kappa| state. WRONG only on a shown counterexample to the eigenvalue, which R1/R2 exclude for the states used. DATA-DEPENDENT is excluded because the conclusion is alpha-independent in the domain.
